chapterNote: Five verses of pure urgency, and the psalm is not new: it is Psalm 40:13-17 lifted out, lightly changed, and given its own title — the same one-word title as Psalm 38, 'to bring to remembrance.' The Psalter is willing to repeat itself when a prayer is short enough to be needed often. Everything in it is fast: hurry to deliver me, hurry to help me; let the ones hunting my life be turned back in disgrace, let the ones enjoying my ruin retreat under their own shame, let the men who say 'Aha, aha!' get their reward. And on the other side, the same speed for joy: let everyone who seeks You be glad, let everyone who loves Your salvation say it out loud and keep saying it — God is great! The last verse is the psalmist's whole position in six words: I am poor and needy. He does not offer God a reason to come other than his own emptiness and God's character — You are my help and my rescuer. And then the last word of all, which is the psalm in miniature: do not delay.

1.text: For the choir director. Of David, to bring to remembrance. O God, come to deliver me; O LORD, hurry to help me!
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm of David, to bring to remembrance [zakar]. Make haste, O God [Elohim], to deliver [natsal] me; make haste [chush] to help ['to my help', ezrah, the KJV margin] me, O LORD [YHWH].
1.notes: Elohim le-hatsileni (H430, H5337): O God, to rescue me — the verb 'hurry' is carried over from the second colon, which is why the KJV supplies 'make haste'; YHWH le-ezrati chushah (H3068, H5833, H2363): LORD, to my help — HURRY. le-hazkir (H2142), 'to bring to remembrance', is the same one-word title as Psalm 38. The psalm is Psalm 40:13-17 lifted out and given its own heading: the Psalter repeats a prayer short enough to be needed often.

2.text: Let those who hunt my life be ashamed and disgraced; let those who delight in my ruin be turned back and humiliated.
2.amp: Let them be ashamed [bosh] and confounded [chapher] that seek [baqash] after my soul [nephesh]: let them be turned backward [achor], and put to confusion [kalam], that desire [chaphets] my hurt [ra].
2.notes: yeboshu ve-yachperu mebaqshe naphshi (H954, H2659, H1245, H5315): let the seekers of my life be SHAMED and abashed — the two shame-verbs the prophets pair (Isaiah 1:29); yissogu achor ve-yikkalmu chaphetse raati (H5472, H268, H3637, H2655, H7451): let those who DELIGHT in my harm be turned back and humiliated. Not destruction: reversal. He asks that they be stopped and embarrassed, which is the mildest imprecation in the Psalter.

3.text: Let those who say, 'Aha! Aha!' turn back because of their own shame.
3.amp: Let them be turned back [shub] for a reward [eqev] of their shame [bosheth] that say [amar], Aha, aha.
3.notes: yashubu al-eqeb boshtam (H7725, H6118, H1322): let them turn back 'on the heel of' their shame — eqev, the heel-word of Jacob's name and Psalm 41:9, here meaning the consequence, what follows on behind; ha-omerim heach heach (H559, H1889): who say 'Aha, aha!' — the sound of a spectator enjoying a fall (cf. Ezekiel 25:3; Psalm 35:21). The psalm asks that their own jeer be the thing that trips them.

4.text: Let all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; and let those who love Your salvation say it again and again: 'God is great!'
4.amp: Let all those that seek [baqash] You rejoice [sus] and be glad [samach] in You: and let such as love [ahab] Your salvation [yeshuah] say [amar] continually [tamid], Let God [Elohim] be magnified [gadal].
4.notes: yasisu ve-yismechu bekha kol-mebaqshekha (H7797, H8055, H1245): let all who seek YOU rejoice and be glad IN YOU — the same verb, baqash, that the enemies used on his life in verse 2, aimed at God instead. ve-yomeru tamid yigdal Elohim ohabe yeshuatekha (H559, H8548, H1431, H157, H3444): and let the lovers of Your salvation say CONTINUALLY, 'God be magnified'. Two kinds of seekers in one psalm, and the difference is what they are hunting.

5.text: But I am poor and needy; O God, hurry to me! You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay.
5.amp: But I am poor [ani — afflicted] and needy [ebyon]: make haste [chush] unto me, O God [Elohim]: You are my help [ezer] and my deliverer [palat]; O LORD [YHWH], make no tarrying [achar — do not delay].
5.notes: va-ani ani ve-ebyon (H6041, H34): but I am afflicted and needy — the only credential he offers, and the one the Psalter keeps saying God answers to (Psalm 40:17; 86:1); Elohim chushah-li (H430, H2363): God, HURRY to me. ezri u-mephalti attah (H5828, H6403): my help and my rescuer are You; YHWH al-teachar (H3068, H309): LORD, do not DELAY. Five verses, four imperatives of speed, and the last word is the psalm in miniature.
